notes.definition: Fungal diseases are communicable diseases caused by fungi. The example you need is rose black spot, a fungal disease of rose plants that causes purple or black spots on the leaves and reduces growth.
explanation: Fungi are one of the four types of pathogen. Many fungi that cause plant disease reproduce by producing huge numbers of tiny spores. Spores are light and are easily carried from plant to plant, which is how fungal diseases spread. The fungal disease you need to know for GCSE is rose black spot.

Rose black spot is a fungal disease where purple or black spots develop on the leaves of rose plants. The infected leaves often turn yellow and drop early, before autumn. This reduces the total area of leaf on the plant. With fewer leaves, and less green tissue on the leaves that remain, the plant absorbs less light and carries out less photosynthesis. Less glucose is made, so the growth of the plant is affected and it produces fewer flowers.

Rose black spot is spread in the environment by water or wind. Spores produced on the infected leaves are carried by the wind or splashed by rain or watering onto the leaves of healthy plants nearby. Wet leaves help the spores infect a new leaf, so the disease is often worse in wet weather and when plants are watered from above.

Rose black spot can be treated by using fungicides and/or removing and destroying the affected leaves. Fungicides are chemicals that kill fungi; they are sprayed onto the plants. Removing infected leaves, including those that have fallen on the ground, and destroying them (for example by burning) removes the source of new spores, so fewer healthy leaves become infected. Infected leaves should not be put on a compost heap, as the fungus could survive and spread again.
keyFacts: Rose black spot is caused by a fungus.
Purple or black spots develop on the leaves.
Infected leaves often turn yellow and drop early.
Growth is affected because photosynthesis is reduced.
Rose black spot is spread in the environment by water or wind.
Fungal spores are carried from infected leaves to healthy leaves.
It is treated using fungicides and/or by removing and destroying affected leaves.
Fungicides are chemicals that kill fungi.

keyTerms.definition: A type of organism that can be a pathogen; plant pathogenic fungi often spread by producing spores.
A fungal disease of roses causing purple or black spots on leaves, which turn yellow and drop early.
A tiny reproductive structure released by a fungus that can be carried by wind or water to start a new infection.
A chemical that kills fungi, used to treat fungal plant diseases.
The process by which plants use light energy to make glucose; reduced when leaves are damaged or lost.

workedExamples.title: Explaining reduced growth
workedExamples.question: Explain why a rose bush with black spot grows less than a healthy rose bush.
steps: Black spot causes purple or black spots on the leaves.
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop early, so the plant has less leaf area.
Less leaf area means less light is absorbed for photosynthesis.
Less glucose is made, so less is available for growth.
workedExamples.answer: Spotted, yellowing leaves fall early, so there is less photosynthesis and less glucose for growth.

workedExamples.title: Analysing a fungicide trial
workedExamples.question: In a trial, untreated rose leaves had a mean of 18 black spots per leaf. Leaves sprayed with fungicide had a mean of 4.5 spots per leaf. Calculate the percentage reduction in spots.
workedExamples.answer: 75% reduction in the number of spots.

workedExamples.title: Choosing a control method
workedExamples.question: A gardener's roses have black spot. Many fallen leaves lie under the bushes. Suggest two things the gardener should do and explain why.
steps: Spray the plants with fungicide, which kills the fungus on the leaves.
Collect and destroy (burn) affected leaves, including fallen ones.
Removing them removes the source of spores, so fewer spores are carried by wind or water to healthy leaves.
workedExamples.answer: Use a fungicide to kill the fungus, and remove and destroy affected leaves so fewer spores spread.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think rose black spot is caused by a virus or bacterium.
misconceptions.right: In fact rose black spot is caused by a fungus, which is why fungicides are used.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the plant suffers because the spots poison it.
misconceptions.right: In fact growth is affected because leaves turn yellow and drop early, reducing photosynthesis.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think antibiotics or pesticides can be used to treat black spot.
misconceptions.right: In fact fungicides are used: antibiotics kill bacteria and insecticides kill insects.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think putting infected leaves on the compost heap gets rid of the disease.
misconceptions.right: In fact affected leaves should be destroyed (for example burnt), otherwise the fungus can survive and spores spread again.

realWorld: Garden centres sell fungicide sprays specifically for black spot and advise spraying in spring before symptoms are bad.
Gardeners water roses at the base rather than over the leaves to reduce rain-splash style spread of spores.
Plant breeders have developed rose varieties that are more resistant to black spot.
Public parks rake up and remove fallen rose leaves in autumn to reduce infection the following year.
examTips: Use the exact spec description: purple or black spots, leaves turn yellow and drop early.
Link the effect to photosynthesis: less leaf area means less photosynthesis, so less glucose for growth.
For spread, say 'by water or wind' and mention spores for full marks in explain questions.
For treatment, give both: fungicides and removing and destroying the affected leaves.
summary: Rose black spot is a fungal disease of roses.
Purple or black spots develop on leaves, which turn yellow and drop early.
Growth is affected because photosynthesis is reduced.
It spreads in the environment by water or wind.
It is treated with fungicides and/or removing and destroying affected leaves.

questions.question: What type of pathogen causes rose black spot?
options: Virus
Bacterium
Fungus
Protist
markScheme: 1 mark: fungus
questions.explanation: Rose black spot is the fungal disease named in the specification. TMV is the plant virus example.

questions.question: Which symptom is seen on a rose plant with black spot?
options: Purple or black spots on the leaves
A mosaic pattern of pale patches on the leaves
White powder on the roots
Swollen, rotting stems
markScheme: 1 mark: purple or black spots on the leaves
questions.explanation: Black spot causes purple or black spots on leaves, which then turn yellow and drop early. A mosaic pattern is caused by TMV.

questions.question: How is rose black spot spread?
options: By sexual contact
By mosquitoes
By eating infected leaves
By water or wind
markScheme: 1 mark: by water or wind
questions.explanation: The fungal spores are spread in the environment by water or wind.

questions.question: Which substance is used to treat rose black spot?
options: Penicillin
Fungicide
Antiretroviral drug
Insecticide
markScheme: 1 mark: fungicide
questions.explanation: Fungicides kill fungi. Penicillin is an antibiotic for bacteria, antiretroviral drugs control HIV and insecticides kill insects.

questions.question: Why does rose black spot reduce the growth of a rose plant?
options: The fungus blocks the roots so water cannot be absorbed
Leaves turn yellow and fall early, so less photosynthesis takes place
The fungus produces toxins that stop respiration
The spots make the leaves too heavy for the stem
markScheme: 1 mark: leaves turn yellow and fall early, so less photosynthesis
questions.explanation: The specification says growth is affected because photosynthesis is reduced. Yellowing and early leaf drop reduce the area of leaf available to absorb light.

questions.question: What happens to many leaves infected with rose black spot?
options: They turn yellow and drop early
They grow larger to make up for the spots
They turn completely white
They stay on the plant all winter
markScheme: 1 mark: they turn yellow and drop early
questions.explanation: Infected leaves often turn yellow and drop early, reducing the leaf area of the plant.

questions.question: A gardener collects fallen rose leaves with black spot. What should be done with them?
options: Spread them around the roses as mulch
Add them to a compost heap
Destroy them, for example by burning
Leave them under the plants to rot
markScheme: 1 mark: destroy them, for example by burning
questions.explanation: Removing and destroying affected leaves removes a source of spores. Leaving them near the plants or composting them allows the fungus to survive and spread again.

options: Rain washes fungicide onto the leaves
Water splashes spores onto healthy leaves, and wet leaves help spores infect
Water kills the rose's leaves, so the fungus grows on dead tissue only
The fungus can only grow in rainwater collected on the soil
markScheme: 1 mark: water splashes spores onto healthy leaves and wet leaves help infection
questions.explanation: Black spot is spread by water; rain splash carries spores between leaves, and wet leaf surfaces help spores to infect.

questions.question: A gardener sprays roses with fungicide but leaves fallen infected leaves on the ground. The disease returns next year. Which is the most likely reason?
options: Fungicides make the fungus reproduce faster
The fallen leaves were a source of spores that infected new leaves
Fungicides only work on bacteria
Rose plants become immune to fungicides
markScheme: 1 mark: fallen leaves were a source of spores
questions.explanation: The fungus survives on fallen leaves and releases spores that are spread by water or wind to new leaves. This is why removing and destroying affected leaves is also needed.

questions.question: Why are fungal spores easily spread between rose plants?
options: They are carried by mosquitoes
They can only travel through the soil
They are tiny and light, so they are carried by wind or splashing water
They are spread when roses are pollinated by bees only
markScheme: 1 mark: tiny and light, carried by wind or water
questions.explanation: Spores are tiny and produced in large numbers, so they are easily carried by wind and water to other plants.

Black spot causes some leaves of a rose bush to drop early.
Table 1 shows information about the rose bush.
Calculate the leaf area remaining for photosynthesis.

headers: Total leaf area before infection in cm²

questions.explanation: 35% of 2400 cm² is 840 cm², so 2400 − 840 = 1560 cm² remains. A common error is to give the area lost (840 cm²) instead of the area remaining.

questions.question:

Calculate the percentage decrease in the number of flowers caused by black spot.
questions.explanation: Use the healthy plant as the original value: 13 ÷ 52 × 100 = 25%. Dividing by 39 gives 33.3%, which is incorrect.

questions.question: Describe the symptoms of rose black spot.
markScheme: 1 mark: purple or black spots develop on the leaves
1 mark: leaves turn yellow and/or drop early
questions.explanation: These are the symptoms described in the specification.

questions.question: Give two ways that rose black spot can be treated.
markScheme: 1 mark: using fungicides
1 mark: removing and destroying the affected leaves
questions.explanation: Fungicides kill the fungus; removing and destroying leaves removes sources of spores.

questions.question: Explain how rose black spot affects the growth of a rose plant.
markScheme: 1 mark: leaves turn yellow / drop early so there is less (green) leaf area
1 mark: so less photosynthesis takes place
1 mark: so less glucose is made for growth
questions.explanation: The chain is: fewer or damaged leaves, less photosynthesis, less glucose, less growth.

questions.question: Explain how rose black spot spreads from one plant to another.
markScheme: 1 mark: the fungus produces spores
1 mark: which are carried by wind or water to other plants
questions.explanation: Spores from infected leaves are carried to healthy leaves by wind or water.

questions.question: Explain why removing and destroying infected leaves reduces the spread of rose black spot.
acceptedAnswers: fewer spores spread to healthy leaves
markScheme: 1 mark: removes the fungus / source of spores
1 mark: so fewer spores are spread by wind or water to healthy leaves
questions.explanation: Each infected leaf releases spores. Removing and destroying leaves means fewer spores reach healthy plants.

questions.question: Suggest why a gardener should water roses at the base of the plant rather than over the leaves.
markScheme: 1 mark: water splashing on leaves can spread spores between leaves
1 mark: keeping leaves dry makes infection less likely
questions.explanation: Black spot spreads by water, so splashing water on leaves helps spread spores and wet leaves are easier to infect.

questions.question: A scientist tests a new fungicide on roses. Suggest two variables she should control so the test is fair.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two: same variety of rose; same age or size of plants; same volume or concentration of fungicide; same growing conditions (light, temperature, watering); same level of infection at the start
questions.explanation: Only the fungicide treatment should differ between groups, so any difference in spots is due to the fungicide.

questions.question: What is a fungicide?
markScheme: 1 mark: a chemical that kills fungi
questions.explanation: The suffix '-cide' means killer, so a fungicide kills fungi.

questions.question: Describe the symptoms of rose black spot and how the disease can be treated.
markScheme: Indicative content: caused by a fungus; purple or black spots develop on leaves; leaves often turn yellow; leaves drop early; growth reduced because photosynthesis reduced; treatment: spraying with fungicides; removing affected leaves; destroying affected leaves (e.g. burning), including fallen leaves.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of symptoms and both treatment methods.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two correct symptoms or treatments.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Full marks need both parts of the question: the symptoms and both treatments named in the specification.

questions.question:
A park has a large rose garden. Many of the roses have rose black spot.
Explain why the disease spreads through the rose garden and how it affects the plants. Evaluate the methods the gardeners could use to control it.
markScheme: Indicative content: fungal pathogen; produces spores; spread by wind and by water (rain splash, watering); roses planted close together so spores easily reach other plants; effects: purple or black spots, leaves turn yellow and drop early, less leaf area, less photosynthesis, less glucose, reduced growth and fewer flowers. Control and evaluation: fungicides kill the fungus but cost money, need repeated application and may harm other organisms; removing and destroying affected leaves removes spore sources but is time-consuming in a large garden and leaves may be missed; combining both is most effective; watering at the base, spacing plants or planting resistant varieties also help.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): clear explanation of spread and effects linked to photosynthesis, with evaluation of control methods giving advantages and disadvantages and a judgement.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains spread or effects with some description of control methods; limited evaluation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about symptoms, spread or control.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Evaluate means weigh up advantages and disadvantages and reach a judgement. The best answers suggest combining fungicides with removing and destroying infected leaves.

questions.question: Compare rose black spot with tobacco mosaic virus (TMV). Include the type of pathogen, the symptoms and how each affects the plant.
markScheme: Indicative content: black spot is caused by a fungus, TMV by a virus; black spot gives purple or black spots on leaves which turn yellow and drop early; TMV gives a mosaic pattern of discolouration on leaves; both reduce photosynthesis and so reduce growth; black spot spread by water or wind; black spot treated with fungicides and removing affected leaves.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear comparison including pathogen type, symptoms and a shared effect on photosynthesis and growth.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct points about one or both diseases with little comparison.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Similarity: both reduce photosynthesis and growth. Differences: pathogen type (fungus versus virus) and symptoms (spots and leaf drop versus mosaic discolouration).
